subject: Isolated GPU scaling playbook & reserved capacity proposal
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@quantamed.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: isolation needs & capacity targets (Quantamed)

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps and assumptions before I put the proposal together: 

Pain points you called out:
- Current in-house inferencing is inconsistent under load; spikes during daily batch scoring are causing 2–5x latency degradation.
- Regulatory requirement to segregate patient-derived inference workloads from other tenants (data isolation + VPC control).
- Predictable unit economics for budgeting (team needs a committed monthly cost + clear burst allowance).

Goals you want to achieve in the next 3–6 months:
- Move production inference for the triage model to a dedicated, isolated pool to eliminate noisy-neighbor effects.
- Support steady-state throughput of ~1k prompt completions/minute with room to burst to 2k/min during peak processing windows.
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime and p99 latency under 200ms for 1.5k-token context.

Assumptions I captured (please flag anything off):
- Model: quantamed/triage-v2 (approx 16B) or an equivalent open-architecture model; we should plan for a 2–3x memory footprint with KV caching in production.
- Encryption: customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys and private VPC peering.
- Procurement: you prefer a single reserved capacity SKU with a monthly commit and a documented burst policy.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Draft a dedicated capacity proposal with three sizing options (conservative, target, and growth) and corresponding cost math.
2) Include an isolation & networking playbook (VPC, subnets, peering checklist, required security controls).
3) Add SLA language and a short ramp/rollout plan (canary → staged traffic shift).

Would you like me to include a 12-month pricing illustration with an optional discount tier tied to a 12-month commit? If so, I’ll loop finance and add a detailed billing appendix.

Thanks — circling back by tomorrow EOD with the draft.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0118

Thanks Camila — this is perfect and captures everything we discussed. A couple clarifications: 

1) The 1k steady-state is for live triage traffic; the batch jobs you heard about run nightly and would be handled during our 1–2 hour maintenance window but should not impact live latency.
2) We will need SOC 2 evidence and an internal audit checklist for the VPC peering configuration (I’ll add this to the security questionnaire).

Yes to the 12-month pricing illustration — would prefer the tiered discount approach. Also please include an expected lead time for provisioning the isolated pool (we need to plan the procurement timeline).

I’ve copied Josh (engineering lead) on this thread — he’ll review the technical details.

Laura Chen

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@quantamed.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool proposal (attached) + provisioning timeline

Laura / Josh —

Attached is the proposal PDF and a compact SLA & metrics spreadsheet. Executive summary below; full math and PO language are in the attachment (Quantamed_Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf).

Executive summary (target configuration):
- Reserved baseline: 4x A100 80GB-class instances (dedicated pool) mapped to 4 inference nodes. Estimated steady-state capacity: ~1,000 prompt completions/min for triage-v2 with 1.5k-token context using Redwood continuous batching + KV prefix cache.
- Burst policy: allow autoscaling to +4 nodes (total 8 nodes) to serve short-duration peaks up to ~2,000 completions/min. Autoscale trigger: sustained 70% GPU utilization for 90s or queue latency > 300ms.
- Isolation & security: dedicated VPC with private peering, customer-managed KMS for disk encryption, audit log export to your S3/Cloud (30-day default retention; can extend). SOC 2 artifacts: we will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report + architecture diagram for your audit team.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime (monthly), p99 serving latency target: 120–180ms for <2k tokens (depends on batch profile). Credit table is in the spreadsheet.
- Pricing: monthly reserved SKU with optional 2-week free burst runway for first 60 days (to assist warm-up and model tuning). 12-month commit appendix included with tiered discounts at 10% (12-mo) and 18% (24-mo).

Operations & rollout recommendation:
- Week 0–2: Provision isolated pool in staging; run perf tests and validation with your sample datasets (we’ll provide a perf template and synthetic load harness).
- Week 3–4: Canary with 10% of live traffic, monitor quality/regression and latency; enable KV cache.
- Week 5: Full traffic shift, enable autoscaling.

Attachments in this message:
- Quantamed_Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
- qa-metrics-and-sla-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If this looks aligned I’ll: 1) prepare a commercial term sheet; 2) loop finance to draft the invoice/PO language; and 3) schedule a technical kickoff with Vivek and your infra team.

Thanks — I’m available for a quick call this afternoon if you want to walk the proposal.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

Camila — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear playbook. This looks good. Two immediate asks: 

1) Please include a one-page procurement-ready term sheet (billing cadence, cancellation terms, and PO language) — our procurement team needs that to start the paperwork.
2) Can Vivek’s team share a short checklist for required firewall rules and CIDR ranges so our networking lead can provision the peering in parallel?

We’ll aim to approve the baseline reserved SKU and start the PO process next week; Josh will confirm the exact date for the technical kickoff.

Laura
